title: China Moves to Lock in a New Edge on Taiwan Before the Next Trump-Xi Summit
gist: Chinese military pressure on Taiwan stayed broadly stable through the first half of 2026 and below end-2025 levels, which the author attributes largely to repeated direct US-China leader meetings. During the May 13-17 Xi-Trump summit daily PLA sorties around Taiwan fell to an average of three, with zero on May 14 and 15 against an H1 average of 7.5, before the PLA resumed with a joint combat readiness patrol on May 19 that Taiwan's defense ministry logged at 24 aircraft.

insights.claim: Chinese military pressure on Taiwan remained generally stable through the first half of 2026 with no major escalation in military aircraft or naval vessel activity, running lower than at the end of 2025.
insights.so_what: A stable-to-lower H1 2026 baseline means Taiwan-risk pricing in regional assets reflects diplomacy, not a structural de-escalation.
insights.quote: China’s military pressure on Taiwan remained generally stable in the first half of 2026, with no major escalation in military aircraft or naval vessel activity.
insights.locator: China’s military pressure on Taiwan remained generally stable
insights.speaker: Di Lu

insights.claim: The daily average of Chinese military aircraft sorties detected around Taiwan in the first half of 2026 was 7.5, providing the baseline against which summit-period suppression is measured.
insights.so_what: 7.5 sorties/day is the reference level for judging whether any future spike is genuine escalation or noise.
insights.quote: the daily average for the first half of 2026 was 7.5 sorties

insights.speaker: Di Lu

themes.theme: Summit diplomacy as a pressure dial

insights.claim: Lower cross-strait tension in early 2026 is attributed largely to the multiple opportunities for direct meetings that U.S. and Chinese leaders arranged during the year.
insights.so_what: Cross-strait calm is contingent on the US-China summit calendar, so a lapse in leader-level meetings is a leading indicator of renewed military pressure.
insights.quote: This owes largely to the multiple opportunities for direct meetings that the U.S. and Chinese leaders arranged in 2026.
insights.locator: Tensions ran lower than at the end of 2025
insights.speaker: Di Lu

insights.claim: During the May 13-17, 2026 summit between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, daily Chinese military aircraft sorties detected around Taiwan fell to an average of three, with zero sorties recorded on both May 14 and May 15.
insights.so_what: Beijing demonstrably throttles PLA air activity to near zero around summits, making sortie counts a real-time read on the state of US-China talks.
insights.quote: daily sorties by Chinese military aircraft detected around Taiwan fell to an average of three, with zero sorties on both May 14 and May 15
insights.locator: For example, during the mid-May 2026 summit
insights.speaker: Di Lu

insights.claim: Two days after the May 2026 Xi-Trump summit concluded, the People's Liberation Army ran a joint combat readiness patrol on May 19 in which Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 24 military aircraft.
insights.so_what: The immediate post-summit rebound shows suppression is tactical and temporary; expect activity to snap back above baseline once diplomatic windows close.
insights.quote: the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) conducted a joint combat readiness patrol on May 19; Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense detected 24 military aircraft that day
insights.speaker: Di Lu
